findings: All three expression-strength variants create 108 upper-lip/body triangle intersections in the open-mouth pose.
The 0.35 mm neutral closure variant also creates 92 intersections at neutral and 39 intersections on frames 20, 33, and 61.
The 0.15 mm and 0.25 mm neutral closure variants keep neutral, smile, and timeline checks at the r1106 collision baseline.
The rendered open pose changes the aperture but does not create a convincing orbicularis-oris deformation; the donor surface reads as a floating cap.
The smile silhouette remains too close to neutral and the upper-lip boundary remains visibly synthetic.
decision: Reject every r1108 variant, retain r1106 as the active offline study, and do not create or promote an r1108 blend.
nextAction: Replace direct world-axis patch offsets with body-surface tangent motion or rebuild the mouth as continuous face topology before further expression work.
